title: Frenemies debuts on the H3 Podcast channel
summary: Ethan and Trisha Paytas launch a weekly co-hosted show blending H3 commentary with Trisha's unfiltered stories. It quickly becomes one of the most watched recurring formats in the H3 universe.

title: Frenemies #39 ends in a production dispute
summary: Frenemies #39 (Talking About Gabbie Hanna) ends in a fight over Q&A production, staffing, creative control, and revenue. Reporting describes a dispute over whether Paytas was talent versus a 50/50 partner. Paytas leaves the set and announces they are stepping down.

title: Ethan publishes his response to the Frenemies breakup
summary: Ethan disputes Paytas's account and explains H3's production costs, the crew's role, and the proposed business structure. Paytas posts rebuttals. Leaked texts from the breakup include antisemitic language ("Jew-y"); Paytas later apologizes. News coverage treats money, ownership, and creative control as the primary public frame.

title: Frenemies merchandise launches after the show ends
summary: Teddy Fresh releases the collaboration that was already in production when Frenemies ended. The launch keeps the show's disputed finances and ownership in public view.

title: Leftovers premieres with Hasan Piker
summary: Ethan and Hasan launch H3's politics-and-culture spinoff. The first episode passes one million views within a day and begins a 61-episode run.

title: Ethan publishes "Content Nuke — Keemstar"
summary: Ethan publishes a 45-minute video criticizing Keemstar's reporting and treatment of other creators. Keemstar responds the next day, and the exchange expands into a sponsor-focused debate across YouTube.

title: The Teddy Fresh–Sisters Apparel hoodie dispute
summary: Ethan and Hila say a pastel color-block hoodie teased by James Charles closely resembles a signature Teddy Fresh design. Charles denies personally copying it and says his team may have independently used the same colorway.

title: Jeff Wittek calls into Frenemies during Vlog Squad coverage
summary: Ethan and Trisha hold an emergency episode about Wittek's response to the Insider investigation and review new footage connected to the night described in the report.

title: Federal court grants H3 a fair-use victory
summary: A federal judge grants summary judgment to Ethan and Hila in Matt Hoss's copyright case, finding their reaction video was fair use. The decision becomes a major reference point in creator copyright debates.

title: Triller files a $50 million copyright suit against H3
summary: Triller Fight Club sues the H3 Podcast, Ethan, and Hila over a clip from the Jake Paul–Ben Askren broadcast and an unlisted copy of the fight. The case begins a prolonged public legal fight.

title: Judge tosses Triller's app-review claims against the Kleins
summary: A Los Angeles judge grants the Kleins' anti-SLAPP motion in Triller's separate case over negative app-store reviews, finding Triller had not shown that H3 directed unlawful conduct.

title: Keemstar responds; the Content Nuke cycle escalates
summary: Keemstar posts a response disputing Ethan's framing. Newsweek reports that G Fuel removed Keemstar from its website and that Keemstar confirmed the sponsorship had ended.

title: Philip DeFranco launches H3's fair-use defense fund
summary: DeFranco opens a GoFundMe for the Kleins' defense against Matt Hoss's copyright suit. The campaign exceeds its $100,000 goal in about a day and draws support from creators across YouTube.

title: H3 revisits James Charles after a new accusation
summary: Off The Rails #94 devotes a segment to a new accusation involving James Charles, continuing the show's recurring coverage of the beauty creator after the 2020 merchandise dispute.

title: Leftovers #61 becomes the show's final episode
summary: Ethan and Hasan spend nearly four hours discussing the October 7 attacks and Israel–Palestine. The show goes on indefinite hiatus after the episode and does not return.

title: Ethan publishes "Twitch Has a Major Problem"
summary: Ethan criticizes Twitch and a TwitchCon panel hosted by Frogan that included Denims. The panelists dispute his interpretation; Twitch suspends five participants two days later for targeted hateful conduct.

title: Ethan releases "Content Nuke — Hasan Piker"
summary: Ethan publishes a feature-length video criticizing his former co-host's politics, moderation, and platforming choices. Hasan and other political streamers respond across Twitch and YouTube.

title: Jeff Wittek sues David Dobrik over the excavator injury
summary: Wittek files a negligence lawsuit seeking damages from Dobrik over the 2020 stunt that fractured his skull. The filing gives the accident previously covered by Frenemies a new legal chapter.

title: Ethan and Hasan debate again on the H3 Show
summary: Hasan calls into H3 Show #143 for a long-form debate revisiting their split, Israel–Palestine, antisemitism, and their former partnership. The conversation is their first extended on-air exchange since 2023.

title: Matt Hoss files his copyright lawsuit against Ethan and Hila
summary: Matt Hosseinzadeh sues the Kleins over their reaction video to his "Bold Guy" sketch. The case puts the cost and uncertainty of YouTube fair-use defenses in public view.

title: H3 responds to reporting on the Vlog Squad
summary: H3 Podcast #240 discusses Insider's reporting on a woman who accused a former Vlog Squad member of rape and examines Dobrik's role in filming the night described.

title: Frenemies responds to David Dobrik's apology
summary: Ethan and Trisha convene another emergency episode after Dobrik posts a second apology addressing the allegations and the culture around his videos.

title: The Frenemies fallout widens into a family crisis
summary: Leaked messages and competing accusations involving Trisha, Moses, Ethan, and Hila move the podcast breakup into the Kleins' extended family. Reporting documents a concurrent family rupture around alleged stealthing claims Moses denied; it does not include an on-record Ethan or Hila statement that they cut contact because of those claims. H3 pauses regular episodes for a week.

title: Ethan removes two Jordan Peterson interviews
summary: Ethan says he removed Peterson's two earlier H3 interviews because he no longer wanted the channel to serve as a gateway to Peterson's views. Peterson responds publicly the next day.

title: YouTube suspends H3 after a Ben Shapiro joke
summary: YouTube removes a Leftovers episode and suspends the channel for a week under its harassment policy after Ethan makes a Holocaust joke about Ben Shapiro.

title: H3 examines the CryptoZoo fallout around Logan Paul
summary: Off The Rails #57 discusses Coffeezilla's CryptoZoo investigation and Logan Paul's response, extending H3's years-long critical coverage of the Paul brothers.

title: Ethan debates Pearl Davis on H3
summary: JustPearlyThings joins Off The Rails #76 for a long debate about gender roles, marriage, and her claims about women. The full exchange becomes one of H3's most-viewed debate episodes.

title: Ethan and xQc debate reaction content
summary: xQc calls into H3TV #86 to debate whether minimally edited reaction uploads exploit smaller creators. The exchange ends without agreement and becomes a flashpoint in "reactgate."

title: Ethan and Hasan hold a second, emotional Israel–Palestine debate
summary: Ethan joins Hasan's Twitch stream for a multi-hour discussion about Zionism, slogans, moderation, and each host's audience. The conversation confirms the depth of their post-Leftovers split.

title: Sneako publicizes H3's debate invitation
summary: Sneako shares H3's private invitation and says he will appear if Ethan completes ten push-ups. The proposed studio debate never takes place.

title: Ethan debates Fresh & Fit
summary: Myron Gaines and Walter Weekes join Off The Rails #108 for a nearly four-hour conversation spanning dating advice, platform bans, and Holocaust denial.

title: Ethan and Sneako clash by FaceTime on Raw Talk
summary: While appearing on Bradley Martyn's podcast, Ethan takes a FaceTime call from Sneako. Their argument turns to Hila's mandatory IDF service and the Israel–Gaza war.

title: Twitch suspends Frogan, Denims, and other panelists
summary: Twitch issues 30-day suspensions for targeted hateful conduct after renewed attention on a TwitchCon "habibi" tier-list panel. Panelists reject Ethan's characterization of the segment.

title: Twitch suspends, then restores, H3's channel
summary: Twitch issues a 30-day suspension after H3 loops the Hasan Content Nuke, citing content that encouraged or glorified extreme violence. The platform restores the channel the next day.

title: iDubbbz revives Content Cop with an H3 episode
summary: iDubbbz publishes his first Content Cop since 2017, criticizing Ethan's recent conduct and featuring Anisa, Hasan, Frogan, and Denims. Ethan reacts live as the video premieres.

title: H3 airs a full response to iDubbbz's Content Cop
summary: H3 Show #137 watches the full video and disputes iDubbbz and Anisa's framing, extending the split between creators who had collaborated throughout the 2010s.

title: H3's company sues Denims and Frogan over Content Nuke reactions
summary: Ted Entertainment files separate copyright complaints alleging that Denims and Frogan rebroadcast nearly all of the Hasan Content Nuke without sufficiently transformative commentary. Both disputes center on fair use.

title: Federal judge rules Denims's reaction was fair use
summary: The district court grants Denims judgment on the pleadings, finding her livestream used the Content Nuke for transformative criticism and did not substitute for the original viewing experience.

title: Ted Entertainment appeals the Denims ruling
summary: The H3 production company files a notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit. The appeal is assigned case number 26-5059, leaving the district-court fair-use judgment in place during review.

title: Ted Entertainment voluntarily dismisses the Frogan case
summary: After a year of litigation, Ted Entertainment dismisses its copyright case against Frogan without prejudice. The docket closes without a ruling on whether her reaction was fair use.

title: Ryan Kavanaugh personally sues Ethan for defamation
summary: Kavanaugh files a separate state-court case alleging that Ethan repeated a retracted accusation about his business practices. The filing begins litigation distinct from Triller's copyright claims.

title: The federal Triller copyright case settles
summary: The parties dismiss all claims and counterclaims with prejudice, with each side bearing its own costs and fees. The settlement closes the federal case filed over the 2021 fight broadcast.

title: Appeals court keeps Kavanaugh's defamation case alive
summary: A California Court of Appeal affirms the denial of Ethan's anti-SLAPP motion. The procedural ruling allows Kavanaugh's claims to continue but does not decide whether Ethan is liable for defamation.

title: Oliver Tree's first H3 Podcast appearance
summary: Oliver Tree joins H3 Podcast #125, the first of several studio visits. Their on-camera hostility becomes a long-running bit around a real off-camera friendship.

title: Hutch joins Ethan to discuss a Hasan doxxing controversy
summary: The early Call of Duty YouTuber sits down with Ethan about accusations that Hasan and others had doxxed creators tied to Progressive Victory, becoming an on-air ally in the feud.

title: Harley Morenstein debuts as an H3 After Dark host
summary: Epic Meal Time's Harley Morenstein co-hosts the relaunched H3 After Dark. Ethan had recruited him for the aftershow, turning a longtime guest into regular crew.

title: Nicol Concilio and Rich Lux share an H3 studio episode
summary: Nicol Concilio asked to come in and talk with Rich Lux, so H3 brought both beauty-community regulars onto H3 Show #307. The episode keeps the makeup-world friends inside the show's orbit.

title: Jeff Wittek is arrested in Miami on drug charges
summary: Wittek, then 21, is arrested in Miami-Dade County on reported trafficking and possession charges. He later says the case was dismissed for lack of a search warrant. In Vlog Squad videos the arrest becomes part of an 'ex-convict' persona.

title: Dobrik's YouTube vlog takes over from Vine
summary: After building an audience on Vine with Liza Koshy, Gabbie Hanna, Jason Nash, and Zane and Heath, Dobrik launches a self-titled YouTube channel in 2015. Recurring friends become the Vlog Squad sitcom-vlog format.

title: The Vlog Squad hits peak guest-star years
summary: By 2016–2017 the rotating cast — David, Natalie, Jason, Zane, Heath, Aaron, Carly, Scotty, Dom, Nick, and others — is a fixture of YouTube, with celebrity drop-ins. Trisha Paytas enters the orbit through Jason Nash.

title: A kissing prank on Seth Francois is published
summary: Dobrik's vlog titled "HE THOUGHT HE WAS KISSING HER!!" shows Francois, who believed he would kiss Corinna Kopf in disguise, kissing Jason Nash instead. Francois later says he did not consent and describes the bit as sexual assault. Vlog Squad members dispute that framing at the time.

title: Paytas later says a hotel-room vlog was filmed without consent
summary: Trisha Paytas alleges that Dobrik hid in a hotel bathroom while she was with Jason Nash and posted "I SNUCK INTO THEIR HOTEL ROOM (SURPRISE)" after she asked him not to. Nash reportedly knew about the prank; Paytas says she did not consent to being filmed nude. Dobrik has not publicly granted her account in detail.

title: Liza Koshy and David Dobrik announce their split
summary: The pair, who dated from late 2015, post a joint video saying they had already separated about six months earlier. Koshy largely exits the Vlog Squad orbit and continues a mainstream career.

title: A group-sex vlog later tied to assault allegations is posted
summary: Dobrik uploads a since-deleted vlog about Dom Zeglaitis inviting women for group sex. In 2021 a woman featured in the video tells Insider she was too drunk to consent and accuses Zeglaitis of rape. Zeglaitis declines comment; Dobrik's attorney denies wrongdoing on his behalf.

title: Jeff Wittek joins the Vlog Squad through Toddy Smith
summary: Mutual friend Toddy Smith introduces Wittek, already posting Jeff's Barbershop, into Dobrik's regular cast. Wittek becomes a central on-camera character before the Utah accident.

title: Casey Neistat begins filming Under the Influence
summary: As Dobrik's posting slows and a Netflix-style pitch is reportedly declined, Neistat starts a feature documentary about the younger YouTuber's fame. The project later absorbs the 2020 accident and 2021 allegations.

title: Jeff Wittek is catastrophically injured on an excavator stunt
summary: While filming a comeback vlog in Utah, Dobrik operates an excavator that swings Wittek on a rope. Wittek collides with the machine and later reports a fractured skull, facial breaks, and lasting eye damage. Heath Hussar injures a shoulder on the trip. Public accounts of a cover story and a Kourtney Kardashian call remain alleged.

title: Nik Keswani tells H3 the Vlog Squad felt like a punching bag
summary: Keswani, known as Big Nick, appears on the H3 Podcast and says mockery of his height and disability during Vlog Squad videos damaged his mental health. He had previously compared the group to a cult.

title: Seth Francois tells H3 the kissing prank was non-consensual
summary: Francois appears on the H3 Podcast and says that after Jason Nash removed the disguise, he realized he had been touched by someone he did not consent to. The interview helps pull the 2017 vlog back into public view.

title: On Frenemies, Paytas details alleged hotel filming and control
summary: Trisha Paytas tells Ethan she did not consent to the hotel-room vlog and that Dobrik pressured the end of her relationship with Jason Nash. The episode sits in both the H3 and Vlog Squad records.

title: Scotty Sire posts, then pulls, a defense of Dobrik
summary: Sire uploads a video defending Dobrik that includes private messages with Francois and is widely called tone-deaf. He later apologizes to anyone who felt he invalidated their story and removes the video.

title: Insider publishes the Durte Dom investigation
summary: Kat Tenbarge reports that a woman in a 2018 Vlog Squad video accuses Dom Zeglaitis of raping her while she was too intoxicated to consent. The article also describes alleged underage alcohol at the party. Zeglaitis declines to comment; Dobrik's lawyer denies wrongdoing.

title: Dobrik posts a first apology that skips the new allegation
summary: The same day as the Insider report, Dobrik releases "Let's talk" on the Views channel. He apologizes to Seth Francois and says he has distanced himself from some former friends, without directly addressing the rape allegation against Zeglaitis.

title: Sponsors exit and Dobrik steps down from Dispo
summary: Dollar Shave Club, SeatGeek, Chipotle, and others cut ties. The New York Times reports Dobrik leaving the photo app he co-founded. Venture backers say they will sever connections to Dispo over the allegations.

title: Jeff Wittek posts "My Truth"
summary: Wittek tries to distance himself from the Insider report, denies buying alcohol for underage guests, and shares a call with reporter Kat Tenbarge. Tenbarge says the video misrepresents their conversation and stands by the reporting.

title: YouTube temporarily demonetizes Dobrik and Zeglaitis
summary: YouTube cites its creator-responsibility policy after the sexual-assault reporting. Dobrik's channels and Zeglaitis's channel lose monetization. Dobrik later returns to posting after a hiatus.

title: Tana Mongeau says she is in therapy over an alleged threesome push
summary: Responding to Paytas, Mongeau writes that Dobrik repeatedly tried to set up group sex involving her, Jason Nash, and Paytas when she was 19. She says she is staying out of drama and is now in therapy. Dobrik has not issued a detailed public reply to that claim.

title: Wittek releases Don't Try This at Home
summary: The documentary shows the excavator accident and, in Jeff's telling, still covers for Dobrik. Later he says the series sugarcoated the story and disputes how Natalie Mariduena framed medical bills and insurance.

title: The remaining squad splits over loyalty, vaccines, and silence
summary: Around Aaron and Carly's wedding, Zane, Heath, and Mariah are reported to skip testing or vaccination requirements. Nick Antonyan later says he ended his friendship with Wittek after Dobrik told him to. Public posts about Wittek's eye are called tone-deaf.

title: Dobrik returns to vlogs without Jeff Wittek
summary: Wittek says on a Patreon livestream that he has not heard from Dobrik after another eye surgery. The absence from new vlogs marks a public break after years of appearing as a core cast member.

title: Wittek airs "Dear David" and alleges unpaid care
summary: On his podcast Wittek calls Dobrik a fake friend, says medical bills were not handled as promised, and claims Natalie texted in ways that framed him as the problem. Dobrik's camp has said costs were covered and the stunt had been Wittek's idea.

title: Views answers the accident with Jason Nash
summary: Dobrik tells Views the Utah day is the worst thing that ever happened to him, takes most of the responsibility, and says he paid tens of thousands in medical costs. He also says Wittek asked him to keep the stunt's origin quiet. Wittek denies that account the next day.

title: Under the Influence premieres at SXSW
summary: Casey Neistat's documentary, reshaped after the Insider investigation and the excavator footage, premieres in Austin. It is not widely released afterward. Reporting later describes Neistat as no longer speaking with Dobrik.

title: Tana Mongeau publicly sides with Jeff Wittek
summary: After the lawsuit news cycle, Mongeau talks with Wittek on Friends with Benefits and chooses his side of the split. Toddy Smith is reported to have screamed at her for doing so. The alignment also pulls Trisha Paytas closer to Wittek.

title: Dobrik opens Doughbrik's Pizza in Los Angeles
summary: The restaurant opening draws crowds even after the Vlog Squad controversies. Dobrik later leans on Snapchat and the pizza brand as his main public work instead of daily vlogs.

title: Jeff, Trisha, and Tana record a public alliance episode
summary: The three creators, once on different sides of Vlog Squad drama, appear together to discuss Dobrik, the accident aftermath, and their overlapping histories. It is a late-era snapshot of who remained aligned against him.

title: Reporting puts a Wittek–Dobrik trial on the 2024 calendar
summary: Coverage in late 2023 describes a trial window in summer 2024 for Wittek's negligence and intentional-tort claims. The date later slips as the case continues.

title: Dobrik returns to YouTube after a long gap
summary: He posts a body-transformation surprise vlog and revives Views with Jason Nash. SeatGeek appears again as a sponsor in the comeback coverage.

title: Wittek and Dobrik dismiss the excavator lawsuit
summary: TMZ reports the $10 million case is over. Wittek later says a former team member failed to tell him that Dobrik's company had already covered a large share of medical bills, and he apologizes for the public confusion. Settlement terms are not disclosed.

title: Paytas registers a YouTube channel
summary: Paytas registers the channel later known as blndsundoll4mj in 2007. Wikipedia says it began as a Quentin Tarantino fan account before shifting into fashion, beauty, and relationship vlogs.

title: Paytas quits Celebrity Big Brother
summary: Paytas leaves the UK Celebrity Big Brother house after 11 days, calling the environment extremely unhealthy. The BBC reports the walkout as the first voluntary exit of that series.

title: Paytas begins a public relationship with Jason Nash
summary: Paytas dates Nash, a Vlog Squad regular, from 2017 into 2019. The relationship pulls Paytas into David Dobrik's orbit and later into reported boundary conflicts over filming and other creators.

title: Paytas posts a breakup video naming Nash and Dobrik
summary: After Dobrik posts videos in which Nash jokes about Tana Mongeau, Paytas uploads an emotional call-out. In a June 2019 Entertainment Tonight interview she says she has not heard from Dobrik and describes the split as explosive.

title: Paytas makes a public gender-identity announcement
summary: In October 2019 Paytas says they are a trans man while also saying they still identify with the gender assigned at birth. Coverage is mixed. In 2021 Paytas says they identify as non-binary and use she/they pronouns, later telling Vulture they had lacked vocabulary in 2019.

title: Paytas and Gabbie Hanna's feud goes public
summary: Metro dates the public feud to a 2019 YouTube video. Reported claims include gossip about Paytas's then-boyfriend and later a failed 2021 podcast sit-down. After Frenemies ends, Hanna posts unused podcast tape and the hashtag #ApologizeToGabbieHanna spreads.

title: Paytas and Ethan Klein trade public insults before Frenemies
summary: Business Insider traces a 2019 feud to Klein criticizing Paytas's appearance and photo editing, and Paytas calling him out for fat-shaming. The pair later appear together on H3 in 2020, which leads into the Bach3lorette bit and Frenemies.

title: Jeffree Star apologizes after alleged Vegas comments
summary: Paytas alleged body-shaming and bullying on a Las Vegas hang with Jeffree Star's circle. Business Insider reports Star later apologized. The trip sits inside a longer friendship fracture with Shane Dawson after Star's hairstylist attacked Paytas and Dawson stayed loyal to Star.

title: Paytas meets Moses Hacmon on H3's Bach3lorette bit
summary: After a February 2020 H3 appearance, the Kleins run a Bachelorette-style segment to find Paytas a date. On March 14 Paytas expresses interest in Hila's brother Moses. Lockdown then moves the pair off-camera; they later quarantine together, which Ethan says he learned about from social media.

title: Alleged Moses bruise photos are said to have been discussed on Frenemies (episode number unpinned)
summary: It is alleged that Paytas struck Moses early in the relationship, leaving bruises, and that Ethan raised private DMs or photos on Frenemies. The episode number is still unpinned: fan threads point to #1; a Cheese Mukbang #9 transcript shows a relationship fight without a clear bruise-photo segment. The podcast continued through #39. Moses's contemporaneous on-record response was not located in the news packet used here.

title: Paytas announces an engagement to Moses Hacmon
summary: On Christmas 2020 Paytas says Hacmon proposed at California's Imperial Sand Dunes during an Aladdin and Jasmine photoshoot, reported as December 18. The announcement is widely covered as they buy a house together.

title: On Frenemies #17, Paytas alleges abuse by a middle-school teacher
summary: In Trisha Was Bullied & It's Not OK, Paytas names a Byron, Illinois, teacher, alleges molestation in middle school, and claims the teacher was later arrested over child sexual abuse material. TikToks urge viewers to Google the name. The arrest detail is later contested; this beat records the on-air allegation, not a later records dispute.

links.label: Business Insider (ep17 claims and later records review)

title: Ethan Klein unlists Frenemies #17 pending clarification
summary: After a September 2021 exposé reported no public arrest record matching the on-air claim and said the named teacher appeared to have died in 2019, Klein tweets that some claims seem to contradict available evidence and unlists the episode, citing stress on the deceased teacher's family. He says he does not believe Paytas would lie and wants clarification. Business Insider also reports no arrest records found. Paytas later says they misspoke about the arrest after being given inaccurate information. That dispute is not a verdict on the abuse allegation itself.

title: Paytas marries Moses Hacmon
summary: The couple marry at the Four Seasons Westlake Village. Coverage describes a black gown and walking down the aisle to My Chemical Romance. Paytas posts announcement vlogs the next day.

title: Daughter Malibu Barbie is born
summary: Paytas and Hacmon announce the birth of their first child, a daughter named Malibu Barbie. CNN reports the Instagram announcement the next day. Paytas had previously said doctors told her she could not conceive naturally.

title: Oversharing with Colleen & Trish is cancelled
summary: Paytas and Colleen Ballinger's short-lived podcast ends after about three episodes. Paytas says leaked messages showed Ballinger sharing Paytas's OnlyFans material to mock her, amid separate grooming allegations against Ballinger that Ballinger denied when Paytas asked.

title: Just Trish launches with Oscar Gracey
summary: Paytas begins Just Trish, co-hosted with Oscar Gracey. Wikipedia says an August 2023 Tana Mongeau episode is the first to pass one million YouTube views, and the show becomes Paytas's main late-career format.

title: Paytas describes early-relationship crises to Rolling Stone
summary: In a March 2024 profile Paytas says that early in the relationship with Moses she drove to his house high, stood naked on his porch, and threatened to kill herself, and that his love motivated later self-work. The passage is a self-description, separate from the unpinned Frenemies bruise-photo beat.

title: Daughter Elvis is born
summary: Paytas and Hacmon welcome a second daughter, Elvis. The Independent reports the name in early June 2024.

title: Paytas appears on Saturday Night Live
summary: Paytas makes a surprise cameo as herself in a Spotify Wrapped parody on the Paul Mescal episode. Coverage notes the appearance years after Ethan Klein joked on Frenemies that he would cut his arm off if she ever made the show.

title: Trisha Paytas' Big Broadway Dream plays the St. James
summary: Paytas stars in a one-night benefit at the St. James Theatre with Sutton Foster, Ben Platt, Joy Woods, and Rachel Zegler. Playbill reports the show also streams live.

title: Son Aquaman Moses Paytas-Hacmon is born
summary: Paytas and Hacmon welcome a third child, a son named Aquaman Moses, on July 12, 2025. People and Entertainment Weekly report the name reveal on Just Trish later that month.

title: Jeffree Star is already a MySpace celebrity
summary: Star, born Jeffrey Lynn Steininger Jr. in 1985, grows up in Orange County and uses MySpace for music, fashion, and photoshoots that draw huge comment counts. Wikipedia dates the public career to 2003.

title: Footage shows Jeffree Star using racial slurs
summary: Clips later traced to about 2004–2006 show Star shouting racial slurs at women on the street. A 2006 MySpace skit jokes about throwing battery acid on a Black woman to lighten her skin. He later says he regrets the videos.

title: Beauty Killer is Jeffree Star's only studio album
summary: Beauty Killer comes out on September 22, 2009, and peaks at number seven on Billboard's Top Electronic Albums chart. Star tours, including Warped Tour, then leaves music in 2013.

title: Jeffree Star says he saw Dahvie Vanity with underage girls
summary: Star tweets that he saw Blood on the Dance Floor's Dahvie Vanity bring underage girls to hotel rooms and calls it illegal. Later posts promote Vanity anyway. In 2020 he tells Chris Hansen the tweets were based on hearsay.

title: Jeffree Star Cosmetics launches liquid lipsticks
summary: Star founds Jeffree Star Cosmetics in November 2014 and posts YouTube videos to sell velour liquid lipsticks. He later says the end of his music career had left him nearly broke.

title: Jeffree Star threatens Makeup Shayla on Twitter
summary: After a Las Vegas beauty event, Star attacks Shayla Mitchell on Twitter and threatens to beat her. Mitchell denies his account of what she said about another influencer. Vulture dates the fight to May 2016.

title: Kat Von D calls out Jeffree Star as old footage resurfaces
summary: Kat Von D accuses her former friend of not paying an artist she introduced, and of racism and bullying. The fight pulls mid-2000s slur footage back into view. Star tweets that he regrets the videos.

title: Jeffree Star feuds with Too Faced's Jerrod Blandino
summary: Star attacks Too Faced co-founder Jerrod Blandino in a public fight about a unicorn palette. Wikipedia records the quarrel alongside his other beauty-industry fights.

title: Jackie Aina anti-hauls Jeffree Star Cosmetics
summary: Aina says she will not support the brand because of Star's racist record and the attack on Shayla Mitchell. Star blocks her, calls her an irrelevant rat, and tweets about her taxes.

title: Jeffree Star posts an apology video titled Racism
summary: Four days after Aina's anti-haul, Star says on camera that the person who made the old remarks was depressed and seeking attention. Critics say the video does not offer amends.

title: Shane Dawson starts The Secret World of Jeffree Star
summary: Dawson's five-part series begins on August 1, 2018, following Star through the beauty business and his old controversies. James Charles and Tati Westbrook are part of the circle the series shows.

title: Dramageddon splits Jeffree Star from Manny MUA's circle
summary: Days after the docuseries, Gabriel Zamora posts a photo with Manny Gutierrez, Laura Lee, and Nikita Dragun that fans read as a shot at Star. Apology videos follow, and subscriber counts drop.

title: Leaked texts draw a public letter from Jackie Aina
summary: Star's former hairstylist posts messages in which Star uses racial slurs, including one about Jackie Aina. Aina writes that she will not excuse the slurs or the campaign against people of color. The same month he is criticized for wearing cornrows and brushing it off.

title: Jeffree Star calls James Charles a danger to society
summary: After Tati Westbrook's Bye Sister video, Star tweets that Nathan banned Charles from their home and that Charles is a danger to society. He also tweets at Charles's teenage brother. Vulture notes that he offers no proof.

title: James Charles posts Jeffree Star's texts in No More Lies
summary: Charles's May 18 video shows messages in which Star accuses him of sexual misconduct. Charles says those relationships were consensual and that Star was threatening to make the claims public.

title: Shane Dawson films a Jeffree Star Cosmetics collaboration
summary: In October 2019 Dawson starts The Beautiful World of Jeffree Star, a series about launching a makeup line with Star. The collaboration later becomes a Morphe product.

title: Jeffree Star apologizes for a Lipstick Nazi website
summary: An archive of Star's old Lipstick Nazi site, including swastikas, resurfaces in June 2020. He apologizes after the images spread. Wikipedia records the site and the apology.

title: Tati Westbrook says Jeffree Star pushed Bye Sister
summary: In Breaking My Silence, Westbrook says Star and Shane Dawson fed her allegations about James Charles and that Dawson offered to help film the video. She also apologizes to Jackie Aina for defending Star.

title: Morphe stops selling Jeffree Star Cosmetics
summary: About ten days after dropping Shane Dawson, Morphe says it will cease commercial activity with Jeffree Star. A cosmetics-account statement says the company is shocked.

title: Jeffree Star posts Doing What's Right
summary: After weeks of silence, Star apologizes to James Charles for joining the hype and does not address the racism allegations. The video points at other news and ends on a product launch, with comments turned off.

title: A report accuses Jeffree Star of assault and hush money
summary: Journalist Kat Tenbarge reports accusations of sexual assault, physical violence, and hush-money offers. An attorney for Star denies the allegations. Wikipedia later notes documents that appear to show a payment to one accuser.

title: Jeffree Star attacks they/them pronouns on a podcast
summary: On Bussin' With the Boys, Star calls they/them pronouns made up and says conservatives like him because he is real. He later tweets that he said what he said. Newsweek covers the defense.

title: Jeffree Star defends Charlie Kirk on a livestream
summary: After Charlie Kirk is killed, Star says on a TikTok Live that Kirk fought for the truth and tells viewers who believe in they/them identities to unfollow. Out.com reports the rant.

title: Jeffree Star says T and Q should leave LGBTQ
summary: On The Skinny Confidential in November 2025, Star says he is not gay, just open, and that T and Q should not be grouped with LGB. Out.com reports the comments.
